clue.text: They aren't given to hide, say, in transports

indicators.note: one word placed in another means its letters are set inside the other's

parts.note: vans are vehicles that transport goods
'say' introduces an example, as e.g. does

explanation.surface: Animals hiding, perhaps for instance, inside lorries on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: VANS holds EG to give VEGANS. 'Hide' is animal skin, not concealment: vegans won't wear leather.
explanation.definitionFit: People following this diet and lifestyle refuse animal products, leather included, so skins are not something they would accept.

clue.text: B of play in play

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word completing Rattigan's play title The Browning ...
second meaning: a rendering or interpretation of a work

explanation.walkthrough: B throughout this puzzle stands for Browning. Terence Rattigan's play The Browning Version is about a schoolmaster's translation of Aeschylus.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names a particular rendering or adaptation, and it is also the second word of the Rattigan title.

clue.text: Associate of B in train or boat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: browning is a colouring sold for this sauce
second meaning: the word in front of train (easy money) and boat (sauce jug)

explanation.walkthrough: With B as Browning, the associate is the meat sauce darkened with gravy browning, a British kitchen product.
explanation.definitionFit: Browning is a caramel colouring used for this sauce, and the word also begins the phrases gravy train and gravy boat.

clue.text: Innovative railway station at centre of spiral

parts.note: something innovative is new
EL is short for an elevated railway, as in Chicago
a post is a station where someone is placed

explanation.surface: A new railway station built in the middle of a spiral layout.
explanation.definitionFit: This upright pillar forms the central support around which the steps of a winding staircase turn.

clue.text: See 6
Ticket to ride? A kiss — well in!

indicators.note: the well goes in, meaning its letters sit inside the kiss

parts.note: a buss is an old word for a kiss
a spa is a mineral spring or well

explanation.surface: A kiss as the price of a ride, with a cheery 'well in!' for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Ticket to Ride is a Beatles song, hence the question mark; buss is an old word for kiss that crosswords love.
explanation.definitionFit: This card lets the holder travel on local buses, often free for pensioners, so it is literally a permit for riding.

clue.text: Change arrangements relating to dance

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a jig is a lively dance

explanation.surface: Reorganising plans for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejig is to reorganise or rearrange something, a verb phrase matching altering the set-up.

clue.text: B, English, with revolutionary rabble at the Ritz

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: a revolution overturns order, so these letters are turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A Browning figure among a revolutionary mob storming the Ritz hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: B is Browning throughout: the poet Elizabeth Barrett married Robert Browning and became Elizabeth Barrett Browning.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet's maiden name was this before marriage made her a Browning, so she is one of the two Browning poets.

clue.text: Reel in the summer when up?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who tots up, a summer being someone who adds figures

explanation.surface: Staggering about in the hot season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but someone who sums; add 'up' and you have one who tots up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger is to walk unsteadily, and one who adds up a column of numbers is jokingly a totter.

clue.text: Bird has to be about doubly kin to B

indicators.note: one thing being about another means it surrounds it

parts.note: the verb taken as written
a rook is a black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A bird somehow related twice over to someone called B.
explanation.walkthrough: BE goes about ROOK. Rupert Brooke shares both initials, R.B., with the poet Robert Browning, hence doubly kin.
explanation.definitionFit: The war poet Rupert Brooke is a fellow poet with the same initials R.B. as Robert Browning, a twofold family resemblance.

clue.text: Cones indicate use of dak, sorrow resulting

indicators.note: the letters resulting from these words form something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Traffic cones show the Indian mail route is in use, and grief follows.
explanation.walkthrough: Dak is the Indian postal or relay transport system. The definition is a description: traffic cones on a road signal this.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange traffic cones on the highway are the familiar sign of repairs being carried out on the carriageway.

clue.text: Place for food and a smoke

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cheap eating place or restaurant

explanation.surface: A café where you can eat and then light up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses the word both for a cheap eatery or bar and for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Happy scene provided by do-it-yourself students

indicators.note: used loosely: the letters are supplied in a new order rather than as they stand

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for home handiwork
L for learner, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A contented picture painted by students doing their own home improvements.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearrangement of DIY is barely signalled; Araucaria often took such liberties.
explanation.definitionFit: This word denotes a peaceful, picturesque rural scene or an extremely pleasant, untroubled episode.

clue.text: Coming into range, a demon drink

indicators.note: letters coming out of a run of words means they are found sitting inside it

parts.note: the run of letters spans these words

explanation.surface: A demon approaching within striking distance.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with citrus fruit juice.

clue.text: Endless impertinence got up to mortify

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut away

parts.note: neck is cheek or nerve, as in brass neck
rose is past tense of rise, to get up

explanation.surface: Endless cheek stood up to humiliate someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mortify' here is the medical sense, of flesh dying, not embarrassing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: In old medical usage, to mortify is for tissue to die, which is exactly what necrosis means.

clue.text: Bill is indeed a peculiar person

definitions.text: Bill is indeed a peculiar person

parts.note: surface reading: a man named Bill really is a strange fellow
setter's reading: the noun for an eccentric, a figure in a play, and a letter written in a bill or deed

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on a word meaning an odd individual, a role on a play's bill, and a written symbol in a deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a real one of these means they are eccentric or memorable, an oddball.

clue.text: Sikh will say what is to follow

indicators.note: to say something is to pronounce it, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: Sikh is pronounced like seek

explanation.surface: A Sikh announcing what comes next.
explanation.definitionFit: A follow-up instalment or later consequence comes after the original, so it is what follows.

clue.text: Thrice prefixed in size of paper, ending in 45 minutes?

indicators.note: placed in another word, the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: quarto is a book or paper size, a sheet folded twice
ter- is the Latin prefix for three times, as in tercentenary

explanation.surface: A cryptic note about something thrice prefixed in a paper size, finishing in three-quarters of an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion splits the paper size after its fourth letter. The question mark flags that the definition describes the time loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is a quarter to the hour means fifteen minutes remain, the clock being at forty-five past.

clue.text: Don't allow Scots lad a weight

definitions.note: short for bantamweight, a boxing weight class

parts.note: to ban is to forbid
Tam is the Scottish form of Tom

explanation.surface: Forbidding a Scottish boy to carry something heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantam is a boxing division for light fighters, so it names a category of body weight.

clue.text: User of B with feature, for example, of the aristocracy in a way

indicators.note: these pieces go in the last word, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: a manner is a way of doing something
the chin is a facial feature
e.g. abbreviates for example
U means upper class, as in U and non-U

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with a distinctive feature who handles B in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: B is Browning, and the Browning is a famous make of machine gun. 'U' for upper class comes from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U.
explanation.definitionFit: The Browning is a well-known make of automatic weapon, so the soldier who fires one uses a Browning.

clue.text: Chap involved with girl left out of the picture

indicators.note: things involved are entangled together, so the letters get jumbled
the abbreviation for left is omitted from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A man getting entangled with a girl and the girl being cut from the photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the picture' looks like a phrase meaning excluded; split it so 'left out' removes L and 'of the picture' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Graphic means relating to drawing or visual art, so it describes things belonging to images.

clue.text: See 18
What householder pays for a dog at present?

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a tenant pays rent for the home

explanation.surface: Asking how much a householder pays to keep a dog right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival: a current matter is one existing at present.
explanation.definitionFit: Current describes what is happening now, the state of affairs in the present time.

clue.text: Bit of neck, namely what may go round it

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
a ruff is a pleated collar worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Part of the neck, and the collar that might encircle it.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, the loose skin by which one grabs a cat or a culprit.

clue.text: Rustic takes tea with western philosopher

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
W abbreviates western
Francis Bacon was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: A country fellow has tea with a philosopher from the west.
explanation.definitionFit: This old dialect word is a contemptuous name for a yokel or country bumpkin.

clue.text: 8's said to be doubly kin to B

indicators.note: what something is said to be depends on how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: the possessive of the poet at 8 sounds like brooks, and a burn is a Scottish brook

explanation.surface: The poet at 8 is reputed to be twice related to B.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is the Scots word for a stream. Robert Burns shares the initials R.B. with Robert Browning, hence doubly kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's national poet Robert Burns has both initials R.B. in common with Robert Browning, another poet.

clue.text: Mount with drum

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the hill in Galilee, site of the Transfiguration
second meaning: a small drum played with a pipe

explanation.surface: A mountain with a drum on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Tabor is a biblical hill in Israel, and a tabor is a small medieval side drum.

clue.text: One of the second water, doubly kin to B

parts.note: B is the second letter, or second class
a lake is a body of water

explanation.surface: Someone 'of the second water', meaning second-rate, yet twice related to B.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the second water' is an idiom for second-rate, which is the misdirection. Admiral Robert Blake shares the initials R.B. with Robert Browning.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral Robert Blake shares both initials with Robert Browning, giving a twofold kinship of name.

clue.text: Speak without reservation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to say aloud, to voice

explanation.surface: Talk frankly and hold nothing back.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to voice words; as an adjective it means total or complete, as in utter nonsense.

clue.text: Dissolving a beer in it to get drunk

indicators.note: something dissolving loses its form, so these letters break up and re-form

parts.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Stirring something into beer to make yourself drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this formal word means a habitual drinker, a person who is intoxicated.

clue.text: Visualise deposits in money?

indicators.note: deposits placed in money means one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service
ores are mineral deposits

explanation.surface: Picturing banked savings sitting in cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To foresee is to picture events before they happen, imagining the future in the mind's eye.

clue.text: Dress right for B and 23

parts.note: a robe is a long dress or gown
RT abbreviates right

explanation.surface: Dressing correctly for B and the man at 23.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning and Robert Burns share this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the shared Christian name of the poets Browning and Burns, both called Robert.
